blocks.text: I can correctly apply word order rules when there are two object nouns in a sentence.
You will also practise pronouncing final [d] and final [b].
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: Pronounced as in ‘und’, the same sound as [t].
Pronounced as in ‘halb’, the same sound as [p].
A word that takes the place of a noun, like ‘it’, ‘you’, ‘she’.
A noun in the accusative case, directly affected by the action of the verb.
A noun in the dative case, indirectly affected by the action of the verb.

blocks.text: A [d] at the end of a word sounds the same as [t].
In other places in a word, [d] sounds the same as English ‘d’.
So [d] is **not** always pronounced like [t]. It depends where it is in the word.
A [b] at the end of a word sounds the same as [p].
In other places in a word, [b] sounds the same as English ‘b’.

blocks.label: What happens in the plural?
blocks.text: When a word ending in final [d] or [b] gets an ending, the sound changes because the letter is not the last one any more: Kleid → Kleider, Hund → Hunde, gelb → gelbe, Verb → Verben.

blocks.q: In which word does [d] sound like English ‘d’ (not like [t])?
blocks.why: In ‘dein’ the [d] is at the start of the word, so it sounds like English ‘d’. In Hand and Land it is the final letter, so it sounds like [t].

blocks.q: In which word does [b] sound like [p]?
blocks.why: In ‘gelb’ the [b] is the last letter, so it sounds like [p]. In bekommen and Beispiel it is at the start, so it sounds like English ‘b’.

blocks.text: Pronouns replace nouns. Their form changes depending on whether the noun is the subject or an object in the sentence.

items: Direct object pronouns (accusative): mich = me, dich = you, ihn = him / it, es = it
Indirect object pronouns (dative): mir = to me, dir = to you, ihr = to her / it, ihm = to him / it

blocks.text: Example: ‘Er lernt Deutsch.’ → ‘Er lernt es.’ ‘Deutsch’ is the direct object, so it is replaced by a direct object pronoun.
**Direct objects** are directly affected by the action of the verb. They are in the accusative case.
**Indirect objects** are indirectly affected by the action of the verb. They are in the dative case.

blocks.label: Which pronoun replaces ‘den Rock’?
blocks.text: ‘Den Rock’ is a masculine accusative noun, so it becomes **ihn**: ‘Das Mädchen mag den Rock.’ → ‘Das Mädchen mag ihn.’

blocks.q: Match each pronoun to its English meaning.
‘Ich sehe den Mann.’ Which pronoun replaces ‘den Mann’?
blocks.why: ‘Den Mann’ is a direct object (accusative), masculine, so the pronoun is ‘ihn’: Ich sehe ihn.

blocks.q: ‘Ich antworte dem Lehrer.’ Which pronoun replaces ‘dem Lehrer’?
blocks.why: ‘Antworten’ takes an indirect object (dative), like ‘Ich antworte dir’. The teacher is a ‘he’, so ‘ihm’: Ich antworte ihm.

slides.title: One object: the usual word order

blocks.text: When a sentence has one object noun, the usual word order is subject, verb, object.
Ich bringe das Buch. Ich helfe der Frau.
When a sentence has both a direct object noun and an indirect object noun, the indirect object noun always comes first.
German: indirect object {first}, then direct object. If there are two objects in a sentence, one of them will be an indirect object.
English word order is more flexible. Both of these are fine in English:

items: I bring the book to the teacher.
I bring the teacher the book.

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: Do not copy English word order. In German, the indirect object (dative) comes before the direct object (accusative): Ich bringe dem Lehrer das Buch.
Tip: identify the direct and indirect object nouns first.

blocks.q: These phrases come from ‘Wir zeigen dem Lehrer das Heft’ and ‘Mia schenkt ihrer Mutter einen Kuchen’. Which are indirect objects and which are direct objects?
Which sentence uses the correct word order?

options: Wir zeigen der Klasse das Buch.
Wir zeigen das Buch der Klasse.
Sie schenkt die Jacke dem Kind.
Sie schenkt dem Kind die Jacke.
Der Lehrer gibt dem Schüler die Antwort.
Der Lehrer gibt die Antwort dem Schüler.
Ich schreibe nette Nachrichten meinem Freund.
Ich schreibe meinem Freund nette Nachrichten.

blocks.text: Ich erkläre meiner Lehrerin meine Fragen. (from Heidi’s text)

blocks.q: Which words are the indirect object in this sentence?
blocks.why: ‘Meiner Lehrerin’ (to my teacher) is in the dative and comes first. ‘Meine Fragen’ (my questions) is the direct object.

blocks.q: In ‘Eine Mutter kocht ihrem Sohn gesundes Essen’, which is the direct object?
blocks.why: The indirect object ‘ihrem Sohn’ comes first. The direct object ‘gesundes Essen’ (healthy food) comes second.

items: Final [d] sounds like [t], as in ‘und’. Final [b] sounds like [p], as in ‘halb’.
Pronouns replace nouns. Their form changes depending on whether the noun is the subject or an object.
Direct objects are in the accusative, e.g. ‘Ich sehe den Mann’. Indirect objects are in the dative, e.g. ‘Ich antworte dir’.
When two object nouns are in a sentence, the indirect object (dative) comes before the direct object (accusative).

flashcards.back:

flashcards.front: Is German word order the same as English when there are two objects?
flashcards.back: No. English can say ‘I bring the book to the teacher’, but German puts the indirect object first: Ich bringe dem Lehrer das Buch.

What is the first thing to do with a sentence with two objects?
flashcards.back: Identify the direct and indirect object nouns first.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: At school: word order in sentences with two objects
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question. For the sentence-ordering questions, write the whole sentence starting with the subject.

questions.prompt: Task A: Which letter completes the German word ‘Stran_’: d or t?
questions.explanation: The word is Strand, spelt with a d, even though a final [d] sounds like [t].

questions.prompt: Task A: Which letter completes the German word ‘Solda_’: d or t?
questions.explanation: The word is Soldat, spelt with a t.

questions.prompt: Task A: Which letter completes the German word ‘Maßsta_’ (Maßstab, scale): b or p?
questions.explanation: The word is Maßstab, spelt with a b; a final [b] sounds like [p].

questions.prompt: Task A: Which letter completes the German word ‘Prinzi_’: b or p?
questions.explanation: The word is Prinzip, spelt with a p.

questions.prompt: Task B: In ‘Ich antworte ihm.’, is ‘ihm’ a direct or an indirect object pronoun?
questions.explanation: ‘Ihm’ (to him / to it) is a dative pronoun, so it is an indirect object pronoun.

questions.prompt: Task B: In ‘Er lernt es.’, the word ‘es’ replaces ‘Deutsch’. Is ‘es’ a direct or an indirect object pronoun?
questions.explanation: ‘Deutsch’ is directly affected by the verb (accusative), so ‘es’ is a direct object pronoun.

questions.prompt: Task C: Put the words in the right order, beginning with the subject pronoun: der Frau / schenkt / Er / einen Gutschein
questions.answer: Er schenkt der Frau einen Gutschein.
accepted: Er schenkt der Frau einen Gutschein
questions.explanation: Subject, verb, then the indirect object (der Frau) before the direct object (einen Gutschein).

questions.prompt: Task C: Put the words in the right order, beginning with the subject pronoun: meinem Bruder / neue Hefte / Sie / kauft
questions.answer: Sie kauft meinem Bruder neue Hefte.
accepted: Sie kauft meinem Bruder neue Hefte
questions.explanation: The indirect object (meinem Bruder) comes before the direct object (neue Hefte).

questions.prompt: Task C: Put the words in the right order, beginning with the subject: gibt / die Antwort / Der Lehrer / dem Schüler
questions.answer: Der Lehrer gibt dem Schüler die Antwort.
accepted: Der Lehrer gibt dem Schüler die Antwort
questions.explanation: The indirect object (dem Schüler) comes before the direct object (die Antwort).

questions.prompt: Task C: Put the words in the right order, beginning with the subject pronoun: unsere Nummer / der Lehrerin / gegeben / Wir / haben
questions.answer: Wir haben der Lehrerin unsere Nummer gegeben.
accepted: Wir haben der Lehrerin unsere Nummer gegeben
questions.explanation: The indirect object (der Lehrerin) comes before the direct object (unsere Nummer).

questions.prompt: Task C: In Heidi’s text, ‘Eine Mutter kocht ihrem Sohn gesundes Essen.’ Copy the indirect object (two words).
questions.explanation: ‘Ihrem Sohn’ is in the dative and comes first; ‘gesundes Essen’ is the direct object.
